Comment: allomorph -a appears on 1sg, 2sg, 1pl pronouns and interrogative tso-. Ergative is overtly marked with -n (rich allomorphy).

1sg: ERG e-n vs. ABS e-a; 1pl: ERG no-n vs. ABS no-a. All persons follow ergative-absolutive alignment. SK is the only Panoan language where ALL personal pronouns follow ergative-absolutive distribution (p.93).
2sg: ERG mi-n vs. ABS mi-a; 2pl: ERG mato-n vs. ABS mato. All second person pronouns follow ergative-absolutive alignment.
3sg: ERG ja-n vs. ABS ja; 3pl: ERG jato-n~jabaon vs. ABS jato~jabo. All third person pronouns follow ergative-absolutive alignment.
Full NPs marked with -n (ergative) vs. zero (absolutive). System is highly consistent and syntactically based, applying regardless of agentivity, volitionality, or animacy of A argument.
Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in imperfective (incompletive -ai) clauses. The only exception is the dedicated progressive construction (VERB-i ik-), which is neutral (see GB409_22).
Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in perfective (completive -ke) clauses without exception.
Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in past tense clauses. No tense-based split reported.
Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in non-past clauses. No tense-based split reported.
Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in indicative clauses. No mood-based split reported for indicative.

Ergative-absolutive alignment maintained in non-indicative moods. The desiderative -kas creates an intransitive construction with both arguments in absolutive, but this is a valency-reducing operation, not a mood-based split per se.
Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in realis clauses. No realis/irrealis split reported.
Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in irrealis clauses. No realis/irrealis split reported.
Ergative marking applies to agentive A arguments.

Crucially, ergative marking is maintained even with non-volitional, non-controller, non-initiator agents (exx. 18-20) and inanimate agents (exx. 21-22). The system is syntactically based, not semantically based.
Ergative marking applies regardless of topicality of A. No discourse-pragmatic split reported for case marking on core arguments.
Ergative marking applies regardless of topicality. No discourse-pragmatic split reported.
Ergative marking applies to animate A arguments.
Ergative marking applies even to inanimate A arguments (e.g. 'rice sack', 'vomit', 'flowing water' as A). This is explicitly highlighted as a notable feature of SK.
Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in main clauses.

Ergative-absolutive alignment applies in subordinate/relative clauses. Internally-headed relative clauses exhibit an absolutive pivot (syntactic ergativity), but case marking on NPs within the relative clause remains ergative-absolutive.

SPLIT: The dedicated progressive construction (VERB-i ik-) triggers neutral case marking (both A and O in absolutive) for most speakers. This is analyzed as a recent reanalysis of a biclausal structure. Some speakers still allow ergative in this construction. This is the only instance of a case-marking split in SK.

Yes. The marker -n (with rich allomorphy) expresses both ergative and genitive functions. For most nouns and pronouns (except 1sg), the ergative and genitive forms are identical (Table 1). The abstract marker -n covers ergative, genitive, instrumental, and other oblique functions.

Yes. The marker -n expresses ergative, genitive, instrumental, and other oblique functions (p.68). Instrumental is expressed by the same -n marker (e.g. jiwi-n 'with a stick', exx. 18, 23-24). Comitative is expressed by a distinct marker -be (e.g. mi-bé 'with you', ex. 46).
